mach-mat.basis: aluminium → 6082-T6 Aluminium Bar (representative machining grade — not a drawing callout); 429 cm³ × 0.0027 kg/cm³ (aluminium, confirmed by engineer)

mach-stock-wt.basis: 278 × 115 mm cut from 65 mm plate (part 270 × 110 × 58: 2.5 mm a side to square the sawn edges + 3 mm saw cut, 1 mm skim a face then the next stocked thickness) = 2078 cm³ of aluminium, 5.611 kg, of which the part is 21%

mach-mat-util.basis: 278 × 115 mm cut from 65 mm plate (part 270 × 110 × 58: 2.5 mm a side to square the sawn edges + 3 mm saw cut, 1 mm skim a face then the next stocked thickness) = 2078 cm³ of aluminium, 5.611 kg, of which the part is 21%

mach-setup-time.basis: 2 fixturing(s) of the volume-cell routing × 45 min change-over (fixture swap, tool offsets, first-off inspection) a batch (45 min engineering-typical, not sourced)

mach-batch-size.basis: 50,000/yr ÷ 20 runs a year, held between 50 and 5,000

mach-setup-mach.basis: cost-ranked 3 routing(s), machine + operator: volume-cell £8.93 (machine £4.67 + operator £4.26; twin-pallet HMC cell at 50,000/yr: 3 direction(s) in 1 clamping(s) on a 4th-axis tombstone + the clamped face, dedicated hydraulic fixture: Horizontal machining centre — 400 mm twin pallet, 4th axis (production cell) £15.11/hr, 2 setup(s) × 45 min / batch 2500 + 7.1 s pallet change per part per fixturing (Okuma MA-4000H 7.1 s, ISO 10791-9 — Okuma MA-4000H brochure (Jul 2025)), 1.2 min load / unload masked by the cut) vs split-3axis £9.73 (machine £3.24 + operator £6.49; 3-fixturing split routing: HAAS VF-2 (3-axis Mill) £9.05/hr + CNC Drilling Centre £6.64/hr, 4 setup(s) × 45 min / batch 2500 + 1.2 min handling per part per setup) vs consolidated-5axis £11.27 (machine £5.89 + operator £5.38; 5-axis: op 10 five sides, op 20 the clamped face: HAAS UMC-500 (5-axis Mill) £17.07/hr, 2 setup(s) × 45 min / batch 2500 + 1.2 min handling per part per setup) → volume-cell, £0.80/part cheaper than split-3axis

mach-reject.basis: 2% machining scrap (first-offs and dimensional rejects) — engineering typical, replace with the supplier's figure

mach-tooling.basis: 4 fixture set(s), one a machine — on the Horizontal machining centre — 400 mm twin pallet, 4th axis (production cell): cycle ÷ OEE 23.1450 min + change-over 0.0360 min = 23.1810 min a part; 23.1810 × 50,000 a year ÷ 60 = 19,318 h; 19,318 h ÷ 6,000 h available = 3.22 machine(s), rounded up — the capacity at this volume; 8 dedicated hydraulic (tombstone) fixture(s) × £12,000 (the volume cell's dedicated fixture; fixture prices engineering-typical toolroom builds, not sourced)

mach-prog-nre.basis: CAM programming and prove-out 9.50 h (1.5 h × 2 fixturing(s) + 0.25 h × 18 feature group(s) + 2 h surfacing) × £33.27/h manufacturing engineer (hours engineering-typical, not sourced); programmed once a fixturing and run on all 4 machines — not repeated a machine

mach-tool-wear.basis: 18.3 min of cutting × £0.0400/min inserts, end mills and drills (aluminium) — not in the machine rate (£/min engineering-typical, not sourced)

UK book 2026-10-10 method (machine added 2026-10-30): machine only (the operator, overhead and margin are added by the costing). Capex £300,000 = ESTIMATE (review round, 4 Nov 2026) — no new list price or award for a named 400 mm twin-pallet HMC was found (the Haas EC-400 price page returned HTTP 403, not bypassed): the floor is a USED Okuma MB-4000H (2021, 400 mm, 2-station APC) asked at US$249,990 = £187,722 (The Equipment Hub listing, read 2026-11-04 — a new machine costs more); a US DLA award for an unsized ’horizontal machining center’ was US$467,682 = £351,192 (2023, model, pallet size and options not in the record); £300,000 is taken between the used floor and the unsized award (CostVision judgement — replace with a dealer quote). It was £185,000 (2019–2023 used EC-400 listings + 25 %), below the used price of the machine whose pallet- and tool-change times the cycle model uses (Low confidence); 13.0 kW (measured machining-centre roughing mean 13 kW (maker study)); 13-yr life (German BMF AfA table, stationary cutting machines 13 yr (a published tax life, used as the economic-life proxy; no UK table found)); maintenance 3%; indirect 5%; finance 4% on half; floor £8,077/yr (the floor of the book’s lathe / 5-axis class, held — not sourced for this cell); £0.182/kWh. At 6,000 h a year × 0.80 utilisation the rate is £15.11/h — a production cell runs three shifts, the economics of a pallet cell (the book’s convention for a three-shift line, as the EV lines); the hours move this rate: at 4,000 h × 0.50 (the book’s job-shop VMC hours) it would be £32.94/h.

UK book 2026-10-10: 17.45 × 2028 h × 1.18 shift = £41,759 gross; + NIC 15% × (gross − 5,000) £5,514 + pension 5% £2,088 + levy 0.5% £209 = £49,569/yr ÷ 1773.4 productive h = £27.95/h. Loading: ASHE 2025 median ×1.053 (ONS regular pay growth) → 2-shift premium 18% (IDR 2025), employer NIC 15% above £5,000 (2026/27), pension 5% (IFS), Apprenticeship Levy 0.5%; 1,773 productive h/yr (39 h × 52 − 28 days − 2.0% sickness). Source: https://www.aspion.co.uk/blog/cnc-machinist-salary-uk-2026-what-operators-setters-programmers-earn-by-region-208 ; https://uk.indeed.com/career/cnc-operator/salaries ; https://careermetrics.co.uk/occupation/5241-electricians-and-electrical-fitters/. Was £26.19/h
